issues: Integrity: no problems found. The diff only adds a warm-start pre-solve before the existing SLSQP solve. That pre-solve uses SLSQP to maximise a randomly weighted sum of radii (weights between 0.7 and 1.3), with the same bounds and non-overlap constraints. There is no file or network access, no pasted coordinates and nothing that reads labels. The random weights come from the existing seeded rng, so runs are repeatable.

Correctness: no bug that makes the result meaningless. The pre-solve result is used only if all its values are finite, and any exception falls back to the original z0. The final packing still goes through the unchanged main solve and the harness validity check.
Performance: the candidate is worse. Its loss is -2.6343 against the incumbent's -2.6360, so the sum of radii is about 0.0017 lower. The provisional reject is consistent with these numbers.

Statistics: there is one run on each side, so no standard deviation can be estimated from the data and z cannot be recomputed. The reported z of -1195.493 implies an assumed noise scale of about 1.4e-6, roughly the stated run-to-run noise floor. A z that large measures that assumed noise, not real seed-to-seed spread. The sign and the reject decision still hold, because a 0.0017 gap is far above the noise floor.
Runtime risk, not a veto: the extra SLSQP call (up to 100 iterations) runs on every restart and adds wall time. Check that the job still finishes within about 4 minutes.
